A_target.statement:
Let $\sequence {Z_n}$ be a [[Definition:Galton-Watson Process|Galton-Watson process]] with $Z_0 = 1$, offspring [[Definition:Probability Generating Function|generating function]] $G$ and mean $m$, with $\map \Pr {\xi = 1} < 1$.
Then the extinction probability $q$ is the smallest root of $\map G s = s$ in $\closedint 0 1$, and $q = 1$ {{iff}} $m \le 1$.

B_source.statement:
Let $f: \closedint 0 1 \to \closedint 0 1$ be [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]] and [[Definition:Increasing Real Function|increasing]].
Then the iterates $\map {f^n} 0$ increase to the least [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed point]] of $f$.

substitutions.the iterates: the probabilities of extinction by generation n

object_map.reformulation: Encode extinction by generation n as an iterate of the generating function started at 0.

validity_conditions: Conditioning on the first generation gives q_(n+1) = G(q_n).
Convexity of G with G'(1) = m decides whether G has a fixed point below 1.
proof_plan:
Let $q_n = \map \Pr {Z_n = 0}$.
Conditioning on the first generation, $q_{n + 1} = \map G {q_n}$ with $q_0 = 0$, so $q_n = \map {G^n} 0$.

$G$ is continuous and increasing on $\closedint 0 1$ with $\map G 1 = 1$.
By the source result, $q_n$ increases to the least fixed point $s^*$ of $G$.
The events $\set {Z_n = 0}$ increase to the extinction event, so $q = \lim q_n = s^*$.
